The single-reference.tsv corpus was generated independently with .NET 10.0.11 in a development-only C# probe, without invoking the original Pascal compiler. Neither the probe nor a managed runtime is installed into the portable application.

Each row contains kind, input, expected IEEE binary32 bits (hex) and expected invariant shortest round-trip text. Float.Parse(NumberStyles.Float, InvariantCulture), BitConverter.SingleToInt32Bits, ToString("R", InvariantCulture), explicit numeric casts, runtime float operators and Enumerable.Sum/Average supplied the expected values. The corpus has 1174 rows: 530 decimal parses, 510 finite bit patterns, 7 double casts, 9 int64 casts, 5 uint64 casts, 7 BigInteger casts, 99 finite arithmetic outcomes, 4 sums and 3 averages. The bit-pattern sample uses System.Random(1729), 512 NextInt64(0, 0x100000000) values with the two nonfinite patterns discarded. Explicit decimal cases straddle binary32 midpoints and underflow boundaries.

This proves binary32 behavior against that independent reference; it does not claim original compiler execution or identical display text across all historical .NET versions. The native profile deliberately rejects NaN/Infinity and checks overflow/division by zero. It uses invariant shortest round-trip formatting. Source overload/conversion evidence is in TreeConverter/SystemLib/StaticSystemLib.cs and bin/Lib/PABCSystem.pas; TestSuite/realsingle1.pas is run unchanged only with the native runner. Static Single.TryParse and Val retain grouped parsing, while TryStrToSingle uses NumberStyles.Float. Product/PartialSum single overloads are not fabricated.
